name: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G)

sources.note: PSI-159 search record, field 'Flight Platform': International Space Station (ISS); Project Type 'Microgravity Investigation'
Challenge brief frames the combustion investigations as microgravity studies aboard the ISS

objective.value: Determine the conditions under which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane and n-pentane, in normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames, over a broad range of stoichiometric mixture fraction (Zst), adiabatic flame temperature (Tad), flow rate and pressure; support the ISS tests with CFD simulations, identify a chemical-kinetics mechanism that matches the measurements, and disseminate the results.

sources.note: PSI-159 detail record, field 'objective' (local data/source/psi/PSI-159.json): determine conditions for cool diffusion flames in propane/n-butane/n-pentane, normal and inverse flames, wide Zst/Tad/flow range; CFD support; kinetic mechanism
ACME overview: observe quasi-steady spherical cool diffusion flames on porous burners with gaseous fuel; support cool-flame kinetics modelling
PSI-159 detail record, fields 'objective' and 'researchImpacts': the study determines cool-diffusion-flame conditions and develops a chemical-kinetics mechanism - fundamental combustion science
ACME overview: ACME is fundamental microgravity research whose secondary objective is spacecraft fire prevention; CFI-G itself is framed as cool-flame kinetics

safety_functions.note: No source labels CFI-G with prevention, detection or suppression; classified fundamental.

relevance_notes.value: The brief identifies CFI-G as the microgravity tests with the highest oxygen concentrations (up to 85% O2 flowing from the spherical burner), directly relevant to the 30% or more O2 / 10.2 psi or less lunar-habitat atmospheres. The investigation is fundamental cool-flame kinetics rather than a suppression or detection test.

sources.note: Challenge brief, 'Spacesuits and oxygen concentration': highest-oxygen microgravity tests were part of ACME CFI-G; lunar habitats expected at 30%+ O2 and 10.2 psi or less
